headline: Deadlocked gains PAL matching routines and external-disc tooling
summary: Contributors can build more of PAL Gladiator from matching C, covering drawing, object data, point transforms, smoothing, table lookups and game state. Matching means the compiled bytes reproduce the original game; the final snapshot records 350,776 of 5,782,424 code bytes, about 6.07% by size, and 4,475 of 18,085 functions. Disc tools can now read an explicitly supplied image outside the checkout (#56).
highlights: Merged batches include PAL drawing wrappers, point transforms, hash lookups and game-state helpers (#57, #60, #72, #75).
The 45-function NTSC-U contribution remains draft #71: PAL mapping is required before merge and PAL retail inputs were unavailable locally.
Further PAL batches in #77, #78 and #79 were opened but did not merge that day.
Research in #73 distinguishes matching C from unmatched reconstruction drafts: generated translated ranges are not counts of decompiled functions.
